title: Parisian Gnocchi in Gorgonzola Sauce
subtitle: with white wine and mustard
description: Light choux-pastry gnocchi poached, chilled, then browned in butter and finished in a white wine and gorgonzola sauce.

steps.text: Pour the water and butter into a pot and bring to the boil over medium heat. Add the flour and stir with a wooden spoon until a dough forms that pulls away from the sides of the pot.

Add the remaining gnocchi ingredients except the eggs and mix vigorously. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing until fully absorbed and you have a uniform batter that comes away from the pot. Remove from the heat.
Bring 5 litres of water to the boil in a large pot and salt lightly. Meanwhile prepare a large bowl with about 4 litres of iced water.

Transfer the batter to a piping bag and cut a small opening in the tip. Pipe small gnocchi into the boiling water, cutting the dough strip against the nozzle with a thin knife each time. The first couple will stick to the knife until it warms up; the rest will go easily.
When the gnocchi float, move them with a slotted spoon into the iced water until completely cold (about 10 minutes). Transfer to a towel.
Melt the butter in a pan, add the gnocchi and brown lightly. Add the white wine and gorgonzola and cook until the cheese melts and the sauce reduces slightly. Season with salt and serve.
